topic: Thongs vs supportive shoes for summer walking

slides.headline: Thongs all summer: good or bad?
slides.sub: Thongs aren't the enemy. It depends on how far and where you walk.

slides.title: Thongs are fine for short trips
slides.body: Beach, pool, a quick walk to the shops: thongs are usually fine. Most feet cope well with short stretches of low support, and going barefoot at times has its place too.

slides.title: Why long walks feel different
slides.body: To keep a thong on, your toes grip with every step. Over long distances, that can tire the feet and calves and irritate the heel or front of the foot.

slides.title: Pick your footwear for the job
slides.body: For long walks, uneven paths or lots of standing, a shoe or sandal with a heel strap and some cushioning is usually more comfortable. Supportive thongs with arch contouring are another option.

slides.title: Build up gradually
slides.body: Went from runners all year to thongs all summer? Heel and arch pain often follow a sudden change. Mix up your footwear and increase thong time gradually.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Heel pain with the first steps in the morning, a sore spot on the top of the foot, swelling or pain that's getting worse is worth an assessment.

caption:
Living in thongs all summer? Here's when they're fine and when your feet might prefer a shoe. 🩴

Thongs are usually fine for the beach, the pool and quick errands. The catch is over longer walks: your toes have to grip every step to keep them on, which can tire your feet and calves.

For long walks, uneven paths or lots of standing, try a sandal with a heel strap or a cushioned shoe, and build up thong time gradually. Heel pain first thing in the morning or a sore spot on the top of your foot is worth getting checked.

story.headline: Thongs for a long walk?
story.body: Save thongs for the beach and short trips. For long walks, grab a sandal with a heel strap.
